result.title: Evaluable Language-Model Treatment Policies for Sepsis Resuscitation via Offline Value-Guided Selection
result.summary: Offline treatment learning must balance imitation, which stays close to logged evidence but ignores outcomes, against value maximisation, which uses outcomes but drifts toward treatments the records cannot verify. Numerical reinforcement learning strikes this balance during training. For large language models (LLMs), directly using sparse retrospective outcomes for fine-tuning raises challenges of delayed credit assignment and limited evidence for alternative treatments. We present R-LLMC, which strikes the balance at inference for sepsis resuscitation. A behaviour-supervised LLM, decoded into an exact distribution over 25 vasopressor-fluid actions, proposes clinician-anchored candidates; an offline critic selects among them by estimated long-term value. The policy has a closed form for off-policy evaluation, and its rationale is written after selection, so explanation cannot steer treatment. In experiments on held-out MIMIC-III patients, R-LLMC exceeded the clinician reference in doubly robust value by +0.214 (95\% CI 0.091-0.300), with fitted Q evaluation agreeing.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 R-LLMC：行为监督的 LLM 解码出 25 种升压药-补液动作上的精确分布以生成贴近临床记录的候选，再由离线 critic 按估计长期价值挑选，理由在选定后撰写，并在 MIMIC-III 留出患者上以双稳健价值评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉 latent 推理无直接关系，但其「候选生成＋离线 critic 价值选择＋事后解释、使解释无法反向影响决策」的分离结构可供核查，可能对应 LVR 中多 latent 假设的筛选、停止决策以及推理状态与解释解耦的问题。
